results.title: A systematic literature review of artificial intelligence in the ...
results.content: ## Journal of Innovation & Knowledge. # A systematic literature review of artificial intelligence in the healthcare sector: Benefits, challenges, methodologies, and functionalities. Administrative and medical processes of the healthcare organizations are rapidly changing because of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Previous studies suggest that AI can raise the quality of services in the healthcare industry. This study presents a systematic review of academic articles on the application of AI in the healthcare sector. After a careful review, the list was filtered down to 180 articles for full analysis to present a classification framework based on four dimensions: AI-enabled healthcare benefits, challenges, methodologies, and functionalities. Implications for future research directions are identified in the areas of value-added healthcare services for medical decision-making, security and privacy for patient data, health monitoring features, and creative IT service delivery models using AI. Published by Elsevier España, S.L.U. on behalf of Journal of Innovation & Knowledge.

results.title: Smart Home Advancements for Health Care and Beyond
results.content: The full papers were divided into time periods and analyzed from 3 perspectives based on the results from Leximancer (Figure 2): (A) technological foundation, (B) their implications for various smart home services, and (C) user experience. User-centered research themes in smart homes, while recognized as important, have limited attention focus compared with technological and service aspects. Discussions since the early 2000s have highlighted the need for a user-centered approach, focusing on specific groups such as the older adults and those with chronic conditions, under themes such as “Elderly” and “Active environment.” However, much of the research has been limited to usability studies that assess how these groups interact with and perceive smart home technologies, with less emphasis on understanding the broader spectrum of user needs and preferences. This study analyzed 5983 smart home papers from the past 20 years, using thematic analysis techniques to discern trends and evolutionary patterns across technology, service, and user perspectives.
